Order No. 06/ Dated: 04th August 2023 The appellants have filed this interlocutory application under section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay of 112 days in filing the present Letters Patent Appeal.
2. In view of the statements made in this interlocutory application, the delay of 112 days in filing this appeal is condoned.
3. I.A. No. 3797 of 2019 is, accordingly, allowed.

4. The State of Jharkhand has challenged the order dated 13 th June 2018 passed by the writ Court by which the order contained in letter no. 2859 (ii) dated 26th October 2009 has been quashed and a direction has been issued to the circle officer at Nagri in the district of Ranchi to issue rent receipt The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... vs Pradip Modi on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81952836/
1 in respect of 16.70 acres land comprised in plot no.1091 within thana no. 236 under khewat no. 5 of khata no. 114.
5.
The lands comprised in plot No. 1091 were transferred to the father of the writ petitioner who is the respondent no. 1 before us.

6. The respondent no. 1 pleaded before the writ Court that by a registered sale-deed dated 8th November 1966 Satyadeo Narayan Tiwary sold a piece of land admeasuring about 16.70 acres to his father and thereafter in Misc. Case No. 188 R 27/ 1983-84 an order for issuing correction slip was issued, whereafter his father continued to pay rent for the subject lands till 1985-86.

The respondent no. 1 has further pleaded that after the death of his father he filed a petition before the circle officer,
Nagri at Ranchi (who was the circle officer concerned at that time) on 03rd February 2006 and in connection thereto Misc. Case No.06 of 2006-07 was initiated by the circle officer at Nagri.

However, the Additional Commissioner at Ranchi by the impugned order contained in letter no.
2859(ii) dated 26th October 2009 issued a direction to act upon the instruction of the Deputy Commissioner at Ranchi who had opined that no rent receipt with respect to the subject lands can be issued to him.

7. Before the writ Court, the State of Jharkhand referred to notification no. 2180R dated 01st July 1955 to lay support to the order contained in 26th October 2009 on the ground that 7.86 acres out of the subject lands fall within the notified forest area and in terms of the notification dated 17th February 2005 issued by the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India the legal status of the lands recorded as "Forest" or "Jungle Jhar" cannot be changed without prior approval of the Central Government.

sentences.text: The State of Jharkhand also turned to "T.N. Godavarman Thirumulkpad Vs. The Union of India & Ors." (1997) 2 SCC 267 to fortify its stand that all forests irrespective of the nature of ownership or classification thereof are covered under the provisions of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and that rent receipts in respect of the subject lands which are recorded as "Bara Jangal" in revenue records cannot be issued.

entities.text: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulkpad Vs. The Union of India & Ors." (1997) 2 SCC 267
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. In T.N. Godavarman Thirumulkpad the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:
"4. The Forest Conservation Act, 1980 was enacted with a view to check further deforestation which ultimately results in ecological imbalance; and therefore, the provisions made therein for the conservation of forests and for matters connected therewith, must apply to all forests irrespective of the nature of ownership or classification thereof.
The word "forest'' must be understood according to its dictionary meaning.

This description covers all statutorily recognised forests,
whether designated as reserved, protected or otherwise for the purpose of Section 2(i) of the Forest Conservation Act. The term "forest land", occurring in Section 2,
will not only include "forest" as understood in the dictionary sense, but also any area recorded as forest in the Government record irrespective of the ownership.
This is how it has to be understood for the purpose of Section 2 of the Act.

The provisions enacted in the Forest Conservation Act, 1980 for the conservation of forests and the matters connected therewith must apply clearly to all forests so understood The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... vs Pradip Modi on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81952836/
2

State of Gujarat and Ors., Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v. State of U.P.,
and recently in the order in Supreme Court Monitoring Committee v. Mussorie Dehradun Development Authority and Ors.

sentences.text: We consider it necessary to reiterate this settled position emerging from the decisions of this court to dispel the doubt, if any, in the perception of any State Government or authority.

This has become necessary also because of the stand taken on behalf of the State of Rajasthan, even at this late stage, relating to permissions granted for mining in such area which is clearly contrary to the decisions of this court.

It is reasonable to assume that any State Government which has failed to appreciate the correct position in law so far, will forthwith correct its stance and take the necessary remedial measures without any further delay."
9.

From the materials on record, it appears that the ex-landlord through a hukumnama dated 30th December 1944 had made chhaparbandi raiyati settlement in favour of Satyadeo Narayan Tiwary in respect of 24-25 acres land at village Balalong on annual rent of Rs.5.50 and the said settlee started paying rent to the ex-landlord.

This also appears from the materials on record that after the vesting the ex- landlord filed return under section 4 of The Bihar Land Reforms Act 1950 for village Balalong which contained a reference about the settlement made in favour of Satyadeo Narayan Tiwary.

There appears no dispute also to the fact that 7.55 acres land out of the settlement made in favour of Satyadeo Narayan Tiwary was acquired in L.A. Case No. 64 of 1961-62 for construction of Hatia dam and in that proceeding of the land acquisition compensation for 7.55 acres land was paid to Hari Singh, Jaganath Ghashi and others after they entered a compromise with Satyadeo Narayan Tiwary.
10.

Furthermore, there is no dispute as to validity of Misc. Case No. 188 R 27/ 1983-84 and Misc.
Case Nos.06 of 2006-07.
There is also no dispute as regards acquisition of 16.70 acres land by the father of the respondent no.1 through a registered sale deed.

11. With the aforesaid legal proceedings the validity of which is not under challenge, in the background, we do not find any justifiable reason to interfere with the writ Court's order and,
accordingly, LPA No.683 of 2018 is dismissed.

12. Consequently, I.A. No. 10262 of 2018 for impleading Forest, Environment and Climate Change,
Govt. of Jharkhand, Ranchi through the Additional Chief Secretary as a party (co-appellant) to this appeal and I.A. No. 10263 of 2018 for stay of the order dated 13.06.2018 stand disposed of.
